question: Should OpenClaw bundle and support a 1Password resolver that launches an external `op` binary with service-account or Connect credentials?
rationale: The functional defects have concrete repair paths, but accepting this nested credential-bearing executable as a bundled OpenClaw trust boundary requires explicit security and product ownership.

options.title: Bundle After Hardening
options.body: Accept the integration after one-process batching, nested executable validation, dependency authorization, compatibility proof, and secops approval.

options.title: Publish Externally
options.body: Keep 1Password on the generic exec-provider surface as an external plugin rather than a bundled plugin.

options.title: Defer Integration
options.body: Wait until external-executable and rate-limit policy are solved more broadly.

recommendation.title: Bundle After Hardening
recommendation.body: Accept the integration after one-process batching, nested executable validation, dependency authorization, compatibility proof, and secops approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The changed SecretRef runtime, protocol contract, and secrets documentation are explicitly security-owned, and the decision concerns credential-bearing code execution.
